provenance.subject: src/strategy/decision.ts
provenance.how: Each vector pins one case of src/strategy/decision.ts against the upstream rule it ports or deliberately departs from. `deterministic` = the port and upstream answer the same on the same synthetic numbers; `port-adapted` = they differ on purpose and the reason is a row in docs/divergence-ledger.md; `upstream-native` = the case is one upstream's own tests or defaults define, and the port happens to agree. Every `upstream.value` below was computed by running google-research/rrsi @ be50316 under python3 at extraction time; the harness recomputes the same value from a transcription of the upstream source, so a transcribed rule that drifts from the measured one fails without python3 being a runtime dependency.

tags.deterministic: port and upstream agree on this input; agreement is mandatory
tags.port-adapted: the port departs from upstream; the vector id must have a row in docs/divergence-ledger.md
tags.upstream-native: upstream's own case; the port agrees, and the upstream value is upstream's measured output

vocabulary.note: The K axis differs on purpose (ADR 0001): upstream tags nine harness components, this port tags the asset classes a candidate really changed. The map below is the port's declared mapping, and it is the reason `novelty.template-class` diverges.

upstream.call: novelty(['skill', 'skill'], {})

vectors.portNote: Mechanism types, not edits (R05): the set deduplicates, so two skill edits are novelty 1.

upstream.call: novelty(['skill', 'client_tool'], {}) — the port's tool maps to client_tool

vectors.portNote: Two structural mechanism classes not previously accepted are 2 (R05).

upstream.call: novelty(['skill'], {'skill': 2})

vectors.portNote: An accepted class is not novel however many accepted edits carry it.

upstream.call: novelty([normalize('prompt', a text-only diff under skills/)], {}) -> novelty(['skill'], {})

vectors.portNote: ADR tightening #5: upstream recovers a component from the diff, so a text edit under a `skills/` path is normalized to `skill` and earns novelty 1. The port has no diff input: a class nobody declared and verified is not a class.

upstream.call: novelty([normalize('client_tool', a real tool diff)], {}) -> novelty(['prompt'], {})

vectors.portNote: ADR tightening #5, the other direction: a real tool change whose file name and text carry no signal from upstream's regex table is downgraded to the non-structural default `prompt`, so upstream loses the novelty the change earned. This is why a declared tag is verified by the candidate adapter against the real diff instead of being recovered from it.

upstream.call: novelty(['prompt'], {}) — a task template has no upstream K member of its own

vectors.portNote: The K axis differs on purpose (ADR 0001): upstream's nine harness components have no `template`, and `prompt` is its default bucket for anything unclassified, so a task template is structural here and non-structural there.

upstream.call: select_round([A(0.7), B(0.6), C(0.3), D(gate_failure=critic_reject)], inc(0.5), S*=0.55, delta=0.05)

vectors.portNote: Upstream rejects C on the S* floor; the port rejects it because a -0.2 gain inside the band cannot pay for a zero cost change. Same verdict on this input, different rule — see `select.sstar-floor.absent` for the input where they part.
Upstream's own cost-blocked case; the port refuses a fortiori (the +25% cap binds long before 8.6).

upstream.call: select_round([A], inc(0.5), S*=0.55, delta=0.05, guard_fn=lambda: ['valid rate fell'])

vectors.portNote: The non-compensating rule in its smallest form: a +0.2 gain that clears the floor and the cost budget still loses to a violated hard constraint.
ADR tightening #2 (counterexample for the +25% cap): beta1 = 40 lets a +5pp gain buy +210% cost, so upstream admits +30%. The port caps the budget at 0.25 and refuses.
The cap is an inclusive ceiling, not a strict bound: +25.0% passes, and it is the largest increase the gaining branch can buy.

upstream.call: select_round([G(0.55, C=None)], inc(0.5, C=1000), S*=0.5, delta=0.02) — relative_cost_change(None, 1000) == 0.0

vectors.portNote: ADR tightening #4 (counterexample for the silent 0.0): upstream turns an unknown cost side into 0.0 and the gaining branch passes on a budget of 2.10. The port refuses.

upstream.call: select_round([H(0.5, C=None, components=[skill, memory])], inc(0.5, C=1000), S*=0.5, delta=0.02) — shaped 0 - 0 + 0.5*2 = +1.0

vectors.portNote: The in-band face of tightening #4: with dC read as 0.0 and nu = 2, upstream's shaped rule is +1.0 and the candidate is admitted with no cost observation at all. The port refuses before the branch is chosen.
A gain inside the band is not a gain: the same +24% cost that passes outside the band (see `select.noise.outside-band.costly`) is refused here.
The band is the whole difference from the previous vector: +0.04 clears it, +0.015 does not.
Cost relief is the currency an in-band candidate pays with, and both sides price it the same way.

upstream.call: cost_rule(0.0, 0.0, 0, 0.02) — shaped 0.0, and the rule is a strict inequality

vectors.portNote: A candidate that changed nothing measurable and cost the same buys nothing, on either side.

upstream.call: cost_rule(0.0, 0.0, 1, 0.02) — shaped 0.5*1 = +0.5 > 0, admitted on novelty alone; the harness maps the two asset classes to [skill, client_tool], so nu = 2 and shaped = +1.0

vectors.portNote: ADR tightening #3 (counterexample for w_n*nu): upstream admits a candidate with no measured gain and no cost relief because it touches two never-accepted structural classes. The port never lets novelty buy admission; the tie it might have broken is broken by slot number instead.

upstream.call: select_round([B(0.7), A(0.7)], ...) — max() over equal S' returns the first in iteration order

vectors.portNote: ADR tightening #3's tie-break (R07: the selection must not depend on completion order): both candidates measured 0.7, so the lowest slot wins. Upstream's argmax returns whichever equal-scoring candidate was iterated first, which is the order the round happened to finish in.

upstream.call: select_round([B(0.7, nu=2), A(0.7, nu=0)], ...) — both admissible, first iterated wins

vectors.portNote: Both admissible and equal on quality: the two-novel-class slot is not preferred. Upstream's in-band term would pay it +w_n*nu, and the previous port's tie-break ranked novelty first.

upstream.call: select_round([D(ev=None), A(0.7)], inc(0.5), ...) — a candidate without a measurement is refused

vectors.portNote: An unmeasured slot is refused with its own reason, and a frozen delta for it changes nothing.

candidates.inadmissible: caliber-mismatch: measured under a different caliber digest

upstream.call: select_round([gate_failure='caliber-mismatch', B(0.6)], ...)

vectors.portNote: The caller's named reason is carried into the outcome verbatim, so a report can say why a high scorer was never compared.

upstream.call: select_round([N(0.9, missing=1), B(0.6)], inc(0.5), ...) — upstream has no missing gate

vectors.portNote: R06: upstream's `missing` is the scorer's obligation (evaluate.py:53 materialises a missing trial as reward 0.0) and only counts (evaluate.py:114); the judge never sees it. The port refuses an incomplete measurement outright, so a candidate cannot win on a run whose denominator was never filled.

upstream.call: select_round([N(0.9, missing=1)], inc(0.5), S*=0.5, delta=0.02)

vectors.portNote: No admissible candidate means winner: null, which keeps the incumbent — even when the only candidate is the one with the missing trial.

The one divergence that is a gap rather than a tightening: upstream refuses S' < S* - delta outright, and S* is not an input of §11's `select`, so a candidate below the round's incumbent can still be admitted for a large enough cost saving (the in-band rate is the caller's exchange rate). If a round wants the S* floor, the caller must say so in `inadmissible` — see the report.

upstream.call: select_round([C(0.7), A(0.6), B(0.8)], ...) — argmax S' over the admissible set

vectors.portNote: The winner is the highest measured quality, whatever order the slots arrived in.
No admissible candidate means winner: null and the incumbent is kept, not that the least bad candidate wins. A +0.01 gain inside the band cannot fund the +20% cost it asks for.
